_what: The asks a workflow step may name that the run's own door answers (the door method itself, its input the door's whole input, bound like any input), and the right each needs, so a workflow row's `records` (the rights its runs hold when tool:run-workflow-definition takes them from the row, trillion-rust from_listed_row) is made from its steps (read-data/derived-records.mjs). An entry with `at` is a right at that door over the thing its input's `id_from` field names; one with `runs_from` adds the tool its input's field names to `runs` (with `host_from`, a tool of the server at that address, keyed `<host>/<tool>` as the engine keys it, trillion-rust ad16db22f); one with neither needs no right (tools:list: every run may list; tools:read: every run may read its own account's runs, as a sweep of stranded runs reads their summaries, Nov 22 2026). A right is made only from a value given in the step; one named from the run's input gets none, so the door refuses it and the ask waits for the person's AI. A tool:... ask needs only the tool's id in `runs`. Every other ask (ai, the person) waits.

fails_on._what: The door's refusal codes that say the step's own call is wrong, so no waiting, right or person can make it go: such a refusal fails the step with the code and the door's words, and the workflow's on_failure path (when it has one) takes it. Any other refusal (a right not granted, a key not held, a busy or unreachable door) leaves the ask waiting with the door's words as its why. Codes from trillion-rust src/tool_runs/tools.rs Failure::code and the account door.
